text: **Every writable field of every entity is settable through the mutation surface, and a field that cannot be written is reported BY NAME.** The burning case is ST0011's `completed`, which is NULL on the estate's one genuinely wrong row and has no field-setter verb today -- the criterion is the completeness of the surface, with the unsettable set as the printed output. **SECOND BURNING CASE (dc 2026-08-18): an AT row's `note`.** It is the only place this contract records WHY a row is where it is, several notes are load-bearing paragraphs, and **the only verbs that touch the row DESTROY it** (issue 0033) -- so the model holds a field the typed API cannot edit, and the sole route is a hand-edit of canon followed by `sync --to-store`. Recorded HERE rather than under a new decision number deliberately: a second home for one requirement is the failure this criterion exists to name. **AND SETTABLE IS NOT THE ONLY TEST (dc 2026-08-18, catching this criterion before it ratified): A VERB THAT WRITES A FIELD AS A DESTRUCTIVE SIDE EFFECT OF DOING SOMETHING ELSE FAILS THIS CRITERION TOO.** `at green|red|na` DO write the row, so a checker asking merely _can every field be set_ passes on `note` while the verb empties it. The criterion is therefore two-sided: every writable field is settable **intentionally**, and no verb silently clears a field it was not asked to change. **AND THE SHARPEST INSTANCE IS THE CLOSING VERB ITSELF (dc): THE VERB THAT RECORDS THE OUTCOME ERASES THE REASONING.** That is worse than a missing verb, because it fires precisely when a row carries the MOST evidence -- **the rows nobody can afford to lose are the ones the closing verb hits hardest.** Demonstrated 2026-08-18: AT-10.11 was greened by hand-editing canon because `intent at green` would have destroyed the note holding the sha, the corpus, the binary hash, the rc=137 kill and the canary control. **THIRD BURNING CASE, AND IT IS BLOCKING A GATE (vc ruling 2026-08-18, on ic's ownership question): AN ATTACHMENT'S CANON RECORD HAS NO NARROW SETTER.** `intent sync` offers only `--to-disk` and `--to-store`, both whole-estate over 57 threads, so a node that edits one instrument cannot update that instrument's canon record without performing a write that can carry every other node's uncommitted worktree into canon. **The consequence is not inconvenience: gating `canon_commit_check.sh` would create a rule whose only compliant order -- sync canon first, then commit file and canon together -- is an operation two of four nodes are forbidden to perform**, and a gate that cannot be satisfied legally is one people learn to bypass. **The remedy is to remove the need for the permission, not to widen it.** Costed honestly: five instrument edits in one afternoon is five cross-node handshakes, and three canon-stale commits landed in the windows between them. **AND THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT IS NOT THE COST, IT IS THAT THE RULE IS CURRENTLY UNFOLLOWABLE (dc 2026-08-18, self-reported before vc found it).** dc's commit `8f652d1b` -- **carrying the document about this very class, including the ordering rule itself** -- committed an attachment without canon, and the instrument then printed dc's own remedy text back at them naming the file. **They could not have complied**: the compliant order is sync-canon-first-then-commit-both, `intent sync` has no operation smaller than all 57 threads, and it is vc's to run. **So that commit is PERMANENTLY DIVERGENT IN HISTORY -- a later sync repairs the NEXT commit and can never reach one already made.** **A rule its own author cannot obey while writing it down is not a discipline problem; it is a missing operation, and no amount of care closes it.** It also settles the gating question by demonstration: gated, dc would have been blocked from committing the document arguing for the gate. **FOURTH INSTANCE, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT AXIS FROM THE FIRST THREE (ic 2026-08-18, who traced the reach before reporting it and then declined to mint into canon while vc was live in the same files): THERE IS NO VERB THAT CREATES AN AC OR AN AT AT ALL.** `intent ac` is list/status/satisfy/unsatisfy/gate/descope/rescope/withdraw/reinstate and `intent at` is list/lint/green/red/na -- **every one transitions a row that ALREADY EXISTS.** Verified by reach rather than inferred from `--help`: no create in `facade.rs`, none in `graphql.rs` or `schema.graphql`, `ingest.rs` never reads `acceptance.md`, and `store.rs` exposes `criteria_of`/`tests_of` as readers. **The first three instances are FIELD completeness; this is ENTITY CREATION, and a surface can be field-complete while offering no way to bring the entity into existence** -- recorded here rather than as a new row for exactly the reason the second instance was, that a second home for one requirement is the failure this criterion exists to name. **AND `acceptance.md` IS A GENERATED VIEW** (`views.rs:385` renders it, `:896` adds it to the write set), **so a criterion authored in the markdown is silently discarded at the next `sync --to-disk`** -- the verb that emptied two views tonight -- and its author will believe they have added it. **The only working path is a hand-edit of `thread.json` followed by `sync --to-store`, which is racy against any peer running the opposite direction.** **Demonstrated by vc the same evening while minting ST0056 AC-03.14: the hand-edit was caught only by a SCHEMA REFUSAL naming `/criteria/118/state/is`, because a `kind: test` criterion's state is computed and not authorable. No verb would have needed telling, and nothing but the schema stood between a hand-written row and a malformed contract.** **SECOND BURNING CASE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-19 (ic measured it and declined to touch the row; vc reproduced independently before ruling).** This row records _the only verbs that touch the row DESTROY it_ and _`intent at green` would have destroyed the note_. **NEITHER REPRODUCES.** `at_set` clones canon, sets `.status`, applies. Driven on AT-04.1 at 1705 note-bytes: `intent at green ST0057 AT-04.1` returned rc=0 and the WHOLE-ROW diff in both directions is ONE LINE -- `"status": "red"` becoming `"status": "green"`. Every other field byte-identical; restored with `at red` and re-diffed to identical. Reach traced rather than inferred from the facade: `render.rs:1033` is the ONLY caller with no second implementation in the CLI, `views.rs:538` renders the note INTO the acceptance view, and `ingest.rs` never reads `acceptance.md`, so the view is write-only and no round trip can lose it. **THE DIAGNOSIS IS WORTH MORE THAN THE CORRECTION (ic): _would have destroyed_ IS A PREDICTION RECORDED IN THE SAME VOICE AS A MEASUREMENT**, and nothing in the row's grammar distinguishes the two, so nothing downstream asked. **AND IT IS THE FIRST OVERSTATEMENT FOUND IN THIS ESTATE ALL DAY.** Every other stale record found on 2026-08-19 UNDERSTATED the work -- four AT notes, three WP statuses, two built-but-`to-write` rows, a whole briefing -- and understatement reads as diligence, so nothing challenges it. This one pointed the other way and survived exactly as long, which retires the comfortable half of that observation. **THE COST WAS REAL AND IT RAN THE WRONG WAY: vc hand-edited canon roughly a dozen times on 2026-08-19 to avoid a destruction that does not happen, and THE HAND-EDIT IS THE MORE DANGEROUS ROUTE** -- this row's own closing sentence records a hand-edit caught only by a SCHEMA REFUSAL naming `/criteria/118/state/is`, where the verb would have needed no telling. **A workaround for a defect that does not exist is not merely wasted effort; it substitutes an unchecked path for a checked one.** **WHAT SURVIVES IS MOST OF THE ROW: the two-sided property stands exactly as stated** -- every writable field settable INTENTIONALLY, and no verb silently clearing a field it was not asked to change -- **because a property is not refuted by one instance failing to reproduce.** The first, third and fourth burning cases are untouched: ST0011's `completed` has no setter, an attachment's canon record has no narrow setter, and no verb creates an AC or an AT at all. **THAT REFUTATION WAS MEASURED ON THE WRONG TOOL, AND vc AND ic MADE THE SAME ERROR INDEPENDENTLY (dc 2026-08-19, who was FIXING the real defect while both of them were refuting it).** **ISSUE 0033 IS REAL, IT WAS IN v2's `bin/intent_acceptance`, AND IT IS NOW FIXED.** The expression was `s|^(- ${esc} .*) -- status:.*|\1 -- status: ${target}|`, whose `.*` after `status:` consumes the note; `:1364` now matches the status as a TOKEN -- `[a-z/-]+`, admitting exactly to-write/red/green/n-a and unable to cross a space -- and CAPTURES AND RE-EMITS the note. A character class rather than an alternation because `|` is that expression's own delimiter. **ic TRACED `facade.rs:2283 at_set`; vc DROVE `native/rust/target/debug/intent at green`. BOTH ARE v3. dc's 2026-08-18 REPORT WAS ABOUT v2.** In an estate where two implementations coexist and a v2 binary refuses a v3 tree at exit 2, **_the verb_ is AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION and neither node named which one.** **THIS IS ic's OWN DISCRIMINATOR LANDING ON BOTH OF THEM: could each instrument have produced the other's finding? No -- they ran ONE METHOD TWICE, agreed, and concluded a TRUE record was false.** Agreement between two readings of one subsystem is evidence of nothing; ic wrote that down this morning and both nodes then walked into it. **AND THE SHARPEST FACT IS THE SUITE'S (dc): TWO BATS TESTS ASSERTED THE DESTRUCTION.** `tests/unit/intent_acceptance_cli.bats:99` runs `grep -E '^- AT-01\.1 .*status: green$'` and asserts success, while the fixture row at `:40` is `- AT-01.1 ... -- status: to-write -- red-first`, which HAS a note -- so **the `$` anchor after `green` passes ONLY WHEN THE NOTE HAS BEEN DESTROYED.** With the fix in and the assertions untouched, exactly those two fail. **THE SUITE DID NOT FAIL TO OBSERVE THE DATA LOSS; IT REQUIRED IT. Twelve green tests over a live data-loss bug were not a contradiction, they were a consequence.** **AND THERE WAS NO READER FOR THE FIELD AT ALL:** the grammar DECLARES `note`, `at_normalise_row` REPAIRS a malformed one, the tool COACHES the author on its delimiter -- three writers, three curators, zero readers -- and `at_note()` reading capture group 6 is new. **A FIELD NOTHING READS CANNOT BE CHECKED BY ANYTHING, which is the whole reason the loss was silent.** dc's own unprompted caveat: removing the new verifier while keeping the fixed substitution fails nothing, so it is defence-in-depth rather than the thing doing the work today. **WHAT NOW STANDS: the defect was REAL in v2 and is fixed; it never existed in v3's `at_set`; so this row's second burning case is a correct account of THE TOOL dc WAS RUNNING and not an argument about the v3 mutation surface this criterion is about.** _Would have destroyed_ was a CORRECT PREDICTION, and vc's charge that it was a prediction wearing a measurement's voice is WITHDRAWN. **ESTATE DAMAGE, MEASURED WITH ITS LIMIT STATED: 66 of 132 ST0056 AT rows carry no note, of which 24 are GREEN and therefore certainly transitioned; ST0057 carries 2, both `n-a`. `acceptance.md` has 130 revisions in git, so recovery is possible in principle rather than impossible as first reported -- but three probed green rows show no note in the last 40 revisions, and NOTHING DISTINGUISHES _the note was destroyed_ FROM _the row never carried one_. That is the POPULATION AT RISK, not the loss.** **FOURTH INSTANCE SPLIT 2026-08-19 (ic, correcting their OWN commit message against their own interest; vc verified the split).** `53cb3f34` claims it _closes the gap AC-08.5 names_. It closes ONE HALF. **SUPERSEDED: _the only working path is a hand-edit of `thread.json` followed by `sync --to-store`, racy against any peer syncing the other way._ `Facade::put(&Address, json)` now creates BOTH an AC and an AT, insert-if-absent, two arms at `facade.rs:2469` and `:2511`, verified by running it. That is a checked, typed, schema-validated route.** **STILL TRUE: _no VERB creates an AC or an AT._ At the CLI nothing does -- `intent ac` and `intent at` still only transition.** So the instance narrows from _no route at all_ to _a service-layer route with no CLI surface_. **AND ic SHIPPED A PIN ASSERTING THE SUPERSEDED HALF, WHICH PASSED WHILE BEING FALSE:** `no_verb_creates_an_acceptance_test_or_criterion` grepped `facade.rs` for `fn at_new`, `fn at_add`, `fn at_create`, `fn ac_new`, `fn ac_add` and asserted none existed -- **and passed, while `put` created both THIRTY LINES AWAY IN THE SAME FILE.** **THE PIN MEASURED A NAME; THE CRITERION IS ABOUT A CAPABILITY, and a capability arriving under an unlisted name is invisible to it.** Identical in shape to the `organize` collision, where a ratification expressed as a string literal cannot distinguish a name being reclaimed from a capability arriving under another one. Replaced with `an_ac_and_an_at_can_be_created_through_the_surface`, which creates rows that do not exist, asserts both kinds land carrying a `note` no transitioning verb could set, and goes RED when the AT insert is removed -- **a creator under ANY name satisfies it and no rename can make it lie.** **THIRD BURNING CASE REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-20, AND THE ERROR IS vc's OWN.** `intent sync` TAKES IDs: `intent sync --to-disk ST0057` returns `ok: extract written for 1 thread(s)`, and the scoped form carried nothing of a peer's in a tree with three of dc's files dirty. **So the clause above -- _both whole-estate over 57 threads_ -- is FALSE, and it was false when it was written.** The consequence drawn from it falls with it: gating `canon_commit_check.sh` does NOT create a rule nobody can obey, because the compliant order -- sync this thread's canon, then commit the file and the canon together -- is an operation every node can perform. **AND IT CONVICTS A COMMIT MADE TWO HOURS BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT:** `17705c76` explains a peer's green riding along in vc's extract by saying there is no operation smaller than the estate. There is. **The whole-estate run was a CHOICE vc did not know they were making.** **WHAT SURVIVES IS MATERIALLY WEAKER AND NO LONGER BLOCKS A GATE:** a narrow setter for ONE attachment's canon record still does not exist -- `sync --to-store ST0057` is thread-scoped, not attachment-scoped -- so the instance narrows from _no operation smaller than the estate_ to _no operation smaller than a thread_. The other three instances are untouched. **AND THE CLASS IS THE ONE THIS ROW KEEPS FINDING: not a wrong measurement, a capability nobody checked for before reasoning from its absence** -- the same shape as the pin that asserted no verb creates an AC while `put` created both thirty lines away in the same file. **FIFTH INSTANCE, AND IT IS THE FIRST BURNING CASE MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED (ic drove it 2026-08-24, `ea84d0ae`; hv ruled the amendment, vc drafted it -- read the wording as vc's and the decision as hv's). LIMB 2 FAILS AT THE THREAD DOOR: 8 OF 8.** Until now every limb-2 instance this row carried was refuted for v3 (the AT `note`) or was about v2's `bin/intent_acceptance`, **so the row read as though the second limb had no live instance in the surface it is about.** It has one. A minimal legal `put` at a thread's address -- the five schema-required fields plus `completed`, the criterion's own first burning case -- **silently cleared the other eight: `slug`, `status_reason`, `acceptance`, `objective`, `context`, `body`, `preamble`, `related`.** **POPULATION STATED SO THE NUMBER IS REPEATABLE:** Thread has 18 fields -- 5 schema-required and therefore always present in a legal body, 4 GRAFTED from the stored row (`wps`, `criteria`, `tests`, `attachments`), and **9 that are neither**. One of the nine was asked for, so the collateral denominator is 8 and the numerator is 8; nothing was partial. **THE GRAFT CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A LIMITATION, and it is the reason the result is worth more than the count:** the four children are provably UNMOVED, four lines from where the nine scalars are not, on the same clone -- **so the eight are a CHOICE about which fields get grafted, and a choice is what a criterion can be failed against.** Had the children moved too, the finding would be the weak _parse-and-replace replaces the document_. **AND THE POSITIVE CONTROL RULES OUT THE OTHER WAY OF BEING WRONG:** `completed` moved to the value asked for, without which a facade refusing the write outright would have left all eight untouched and satisfied every other assertion -- a green that is a fact about the harness. **THE SHARPEST FIELD IS `related`, AND THE ARM'S OWN COMMENT SUPPLIES IT:** _`related` is deliberately NOT in this list: it has no address of its own, so the thread door is the only door it has._ **So the thread door is simultaneously `related`'s only door and the one that empties it.** `context`, `body` and `preamble` are load-bearing prose, which is this row's `note` shape again: **the rows carrying the most evidence are the ones the write hits hardest.** **NOT A LIVE DATA-LOSS BUG, AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING:** `put` has 17 call sites, all tests, `intent put` is an unrecognised subcommand, and `sync` carries the WHOLE document so it structurally cannot present the minimal body this needs -- **exposure is zero because no production path exists, not because the write is checked.** **THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN LIMIT, DISCLOSED BY ITS AUTHOR AND RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN ONLY IN ITS NOTE: it asserts the collateral set equals a DECLARED LITERAL.** That is the drift-detector shape, correct for a REPORTING instrument -- it reds in both directions if the set moves -- **and it is NOT the biconditional cover fix, which remains routed and unbuilt.** Recorded in the criterion because **a measurement whose limits live only in its author's session becomes a gate the moment that session ends.** **AND ONE THING THIS ROW WAS NEVER GUILTY OF, CLEARED HERE BECAUSE THE RETRACTION IS PART OF THE RECORD:** the phrase _no write path at all_ is `facade.rs`'s ruling COMMENT and has never been this criterion's wording. cc refuted it (a canon edit plus `sync --to-store` IS a write path, and six scalars survive that round trip intact) -- **but this row says `completed` has no FIELD-SETTER VERB, and neither door is one: the addressable door is a whole-document parse plus a four-child graft, and the sync door is a whole-document authored replace.** The criterion stands as written; **what fell was a sentence in a comment, and that comment carries two defects in opposite directions in one paragraph -- it OVERSTATES an absence and OVERCLAIMS a property (`never a partially-defaulted document`, true of the four lines beneath it and false of the nine it does not reach).** **SIXTH INSTANCE, AND IT IS THE DENOMINATOR ITSELF RATHER THAN A CASE (cc found it 2026-08-25 and ESCALATED RATHER THAN BUILDING; vc ruled; ic had supplied the diagnosis one axis over the day before; cc then corrected the ruling twice, once by independent derivation and once on a point vc had no view of).** **`Issue.body` IS A DECLARED SCHEMA FIELD THAT NEITHER DOOR CAN WRITE**, and `settable_fields` (`facade.rs:4388`) refuses `Issue` at its `other =>` arm while the address sweep calls `E::Issue { .. }` `Reachable` -- true, and an ADDRESS-axis fact. **THE INSTRUMENT ANSWERS A NARROWER QUESTION THAN THE CRITERION IT SERVES, AND CANNOT SEE THE GAP BY CONSTRUCTION**: `declared_reach()` is about addresses, and this row's subject is *every writable FIELD of every entity*. That is ic's own formulation of the door-blindness class, landing one axis over on the instrument that was supposed to close this row. **THE RULING (vc, as this row's contract-holder -- not hv, and recorded as vc's): LIMB 1'S POPULATION IS INDEXED BY MODEL TYPE, NOT BY ADDRESS FORM.** The 13 `address::Entity` forms and the field-axis population are DIFFERENT SETS, and conflating them is the whole of the defect. Of the 13: **4 are COLLECTIONS** (`Threads`, `Issues`, `WpCollection`, `AcCollection`) -- a collection has membership, not fields -- **zero rows**; **2 are APPEND-ONLY LOGS** (`Event`, `NodeInbox`, D53) -- rows are appended whole, there is no field to set -- **zero rows**; **`Node` has no reified model type at all** (see the split below) -- **zero rows**; and **6 carry fields**: `Thread` 18, `WorkPackage` 9, `Criterion` 4, `AcceptanceTest` 8, `Attachment` 5, `Issue` 10 (counted at source by cc). **`settable_fields` COVERS 4 OF THE 6** -- `Attachment` and `Issue` fall to `other =>`. **SO cc's INDEPENDENT CONCLUSION WAS RIGHT AND NOW IT HAS A REASON: closing limb 1's four ADDRESS forms would not close limb 1, because THEY WERE NEVER IN LIMB 1'S POPULATION.** cc reached it from the other end and stopped without being able to say why, which is not the same as being right for the reason -- their words, and the distinction is why they escalated instead of building. **AND THE SECOND CLAUSE IS WHAT CONVERTS THIS FROM A SCOPING GAP INTO A VIOLATION.** This row reads *a field that cannot be written is reported BY NAME*. **A REFUSAL BY FORM NAMES THE ENTITY AND NEVER THE FIELD**, so for `Attachment` and `Issue` every field is simultaneously unsettable AND unreported -- failing both clauses at once -- while the sweep reads green throughout. **cc SHARPENED THAT AND IT IS WORSE THAN vc STATED: THE REFUSAL DOES NOT MERELY OMIT THE FIELD, IT MISINFORMS ABOUT THE ENTITY.** The `other =>` arm's stated reason is *"an attachment's body is its content, and the rest are collections or append-only logs"* -- **and `Issue` is NEITHER.** An operator refused on `intent:///issues/0081` is told the thing they addressed is a collection or a log. **That is worse than no reason at all, because it reads as a considered explanation**, and it is this estate's recurring shape once more: a true-sounding statement about a set nobody had re-counted. **The `why` is false today independently of AC-08.5 and is corrected on those grounds.** **THE REMEDY IS SYMMETRIC AND CHOSEN PER ENTITY:** either a real field-setter arm, or a `settable_fields` arm returning the settable set with `unsettable()` naming the rest and a stated reason. **Both satisfy the criterion; neither needs a new door.** `unsettable()` at `:5251` carries an outer `_ => None` that is currently unreachable dead ground for exactly the refused set, so reaching it is part of the work. **THE RULING CARRIES A BUILD CONSTRAINT, AND IT EXISTS BECAUSE vc NEARLY SHIPPED A FIFTH INSTANCE OF THE DAY'S OWN CLASS INTO THE FIX FOR THE FOURTH.** Indexing the population by model type makes `Node` invisible to this row **by construction** -- and it would STAY invisible when WP-14 gives it a model, unless something re-derives. **That is a guard whose scope excludes a case it will later need to catch, which reads green the entire time.** So: **THE POPULATION IS DERIVED FROM THE MODEL AND NEVER ENUMERATED IN PROSE, AND THE POPULATION SIZE IS PINNED AGAINST A DECLARED LITERAL THAT REDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Derive the partition; pin the population. **The two halves want opposite treatments and that is not an inconsistency** -- growth in the partition is ordinary, growth in the population must be ANNOUNCED. ic's drift-detector shape, whose limit ic disclosed themselves as *correct for a REPORTING instrument*, is on the population axis not a limitation but the right answer. **`Node` IS SPLIT, AND THE SPLIT IS ITSELF THE RULING (cc's catch, against vc's first pass).** vc's correction disposed of `Node` by observing it has no model type and moving on -- **which SETTLED A QUESTION HELD ON hv BY INCLUSION RATHER THAN BY DECISION**, a defect in how the ruling was made rather than in its content. What stands: **`Node` contributes ZERO ROWS to this row's field axis today** -- a MEASUREMENT, not a scope call, because `schema_properties::<Node>()` cannot be written when no type exists to derive from (`pub struct Node` returns nothing in any crate; `facade.rs` mentions it zero times; `address.rs:666` gives it no view path). **What is NOT ruled and stays with hv: whether the model should carry a `Node` type at all.** That is ST0056/WP-14's scope and a larger piece than this row. **THE DEFERRAL COSTS NOTHING ONLY BECAUSE OF THE PINNED POPULATION: if WP-14 lands a `Node` model, this row's cover goes RED and says so.** Without that clause, deferring would have been the guard-scope failure a fourth time in one day. **AND THE FINDING UNDER THE FINDING: THREE READINGS OF `Node` WERE LIVE IN THE ESTATE AND NONE CITED EACH OTHER** -- vc's (in-population, wrong, retracted within the hour), cc's (not field-carrying, held on hv since 2026-08-24), and ic's sweep at `:569` (`NotBuiltYet`, neither `NeverByRuling` nor field-carrying). **They agree on the operative outcome and differ on the reason and the status, which is exactly the configuration in which three nodes can each be confident and the estate still has no answer.** Recorded together HERE rather than left in three sessions, for the reason this row states about itself: a second home for one requirement is the failure this criterion exists to name. **AND THE RULING GREW A CONTRACT CLAUSE UNDER ic's QUESTION, WHICH IS THE ONE PART OF THIS NOBODY HAD A POSITION ON (ic asked 2026-08-25 and declined to assume it; vc ruled; the deciding text was already in cc's own doc comment).** Clause 2 requires an unwritable field to be *reported BY NAME*, so for `Attachment` and `Issue` the refusal must move from the entity level to the FIELD level -- and `Unsettable`'s vocabulary is three variants, `Identity` / `Machine(verbs)` / `Child(segment)`. ic's question was whether every field of those two can be expressed in that vocabulary, or whether a fourth variant is needed -- **a contract change, and correctly routed rather than assumed.** **THE TEST IS NOT _IS THIS FIELD UNSETTABLE_, IT IS _IS THERE A REAL REMEDY TO NAME_, and `Unsettable`'s own doc comment supplies it:** *a name with no remedy sends the operator to a hand-edit of canon -- which is the route this criterion exists to retire. **"You cannot" is not what the criterion asked for.*** **(A) A FOURTH VARIANT IS WARRANTED, AND IT IS NOT A LOOSENING. `Unsettable::Derived(source)`.** `Attachment` is `path`, `text`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `blob`; **`bytes` and `sha256` FOLLOW the content.** No verb sets them and none should -- **a checksum set independently of the thing it checksums is incoherence rather than a feature** -- but their remedy is real and nameable, *set `text`; this follows*. That satisfies clause 2 on its own terms, so it belongs INSIDE the vocabulary. **(B) AND THE CASE THAT LOOKED LIKE THE FOURTH VARIANT IS A GAP INSTEAD, WHICH REVERSES A STEER vc HAD ALREADY GIVEN cc. `Issue.body` MUST BECOME SETTABLE.** vc pointed cc at `Unsettable::Machine` *naming the real route*; **there is no real route to name.** Driven: `issues` is `list|add|show|close|open`, `add` takes `<TITLE>` and `--severity`, `close`/`open` move status, `put` reaches the address and refuses by name -- **nothing writes `body`, ever.** So `Machine(...)` would have to name a verb that does not set the field, **which is cc's own false-`why` finding reproduced one level down and this time authored deliberately.** **A FALSE REMEDY IS WORSE THAN A FALSE REASON, BECAUSE THE OPERATOR ACTS ON IT.** `body` gets a setter -- a narrow arm, `issues add --body`, or `issues edit`, cc's choice. **AND THE ESTATE WAS ALREADY PAYING FOR IT IN A FORM NOBODY CONNECTED: cc's 287-character issue title, the widest in the corpus and the one that set every row's width in the output-shape defect, was long BECAUSE `body` is unwritable.** The UI defect and this row's gap are one fact seen twice, five hours apart, by the same node. **THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN TRAP, FOUND BY ic ONE LEVEL BELOW WHERE vc NAMED IT, AND IT WOULD HAVE READ GREEN.** `schema_properties` (`facade.rs:5199`) returns an EMPTY SET for anything but the four covered forms, **so a settable/unsettable partition built on it is VACUOUSLY SATISFIED for `Attachment` and `Issue`** -- *0 settable, 0 unsettable, partition holds*. **That is this board's own standing watch-out arriving as a live trap inside the instrument built to close this row: _ask which population a control can actually see, and measure it; an empty population returns 0 with, 0 without._** **ic's remedy is stronger than a guard against it: assert through TRAIT BOUNDS and real calls rather than by scanning source.** `schema_properties<T: schemars::JsonSchema>` is a bound the call site already type-checks, **so the compiler has already answered the question a grep over declarations can only approximate -- and a type-checked call site cannot go stale.** **ONE MORE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE CONTROL ON EVERYTHING ABOVE: ic's OWN PROBE RETURNED A FALSE FINDING AND ic CAUGHT IT AGAINST THEIR OWN INTEREST.** It reported `Criterion` as lacking a `JsonSchema` derive -- **two passes blind in the same place for two different reasons**, a fixed 6-line lookback against a 17-line attribute block, then a walk-back that could not read multi-line attribute continuations. `Criterion` derives it at `model.rs:986`. **All six models derive it;
